chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Emmett Berry replaces Dizzy in Kirby's band
summary: Shavers brings in trumpeter Emmett Berry, whom Leeman praises as a swinging reader who later worked with Basie.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: guys, you know, and that's when he was going through his little salt peanuts -- he was developing that routine, it was just about that era. So they didn't know who to get and Charlie Shavers got Emmett Berry, God bless him.
Well, he and I had been friends over the years.
Trumpet -- a great trumpet player, and he didn't get enough to play with Basie to become -- I think he took Buck's place, Buck Clayton's place at one time.

On trumpet, yes, in the Basie band. When the Basie band was developed, after they were well known. But Emmett could read more than anybody would give him credit for, along with being a swinging trumpet player -- and a charming, beautiful, wonderful man.
And I have to keep saying this, because some people were just so close to me.
This is still Kirby's band. Dizzy didn't want any part of it.
